Subject: FlowHealth dedicated capacity onboarding — regional capacity & burst policy choices

Hi team,

Following the signed order (DH-2026-1147) — quick handoff and alignment note for FlowHealth's Dedicated capacity onboarding. Key customer asks we need to resolve in this thread before we open the provisioning ticket:

- Primary region preference: FlowHealth has offices in SF and Berlin. They want EU data residency for PHI workloads; they asked whether we can put primary pools in eu-west-1 with US failover.
- Autoscale/Burst policy: They want predictable latency under spiky workloads (batch inference windows at 09:00 UTC and 17:00 UTC). They asked for burst lanes that allow short-lived capacity increases without breaking the committed baseline.
- Staging / canary: They want a 48-hour canary and a plan to rollback to hosted model variants if pool health degrades.

Attachments: FlowHealth_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (SOW with target SLA and acceptance criteria).

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica — own onboarding plan and CS acceptance criteria.
2) Karthik & Rishi — propose region/capacity layout, autoscale thresholds, and burst gating by EOD Thu (Nov 19).
3) FlowHealth (Olivia/Samir) — confirm EU primary vs US primary preference and list compliance deliverables needed for canary.

Call to action: Can we get technical recs + cost tradeoffs by Thu EOD? I'll schedule a 30-min sync Fri morning if needed.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Thanks, Laura — I'll take point on CS onboarding. A few clarifying Qs from my side before we finalize ops items:

- Acceptance criteria for canary: do we want 95th pct latency <= 200ms for the canary window, or relax to 300ms while we tune batching?

Monica / team — technical recs below. High level: recommend EU primary pool with US warm-standby for PHI workloads, plus a user-configurable burst lane for scheduled spikes.

Recommended layout:
- Primary compute: eu-west-1 (4x A100-80GB equivalent nodes to start) assigned to PHI tenant.
- Warm-standby: us-west-2 (2x A100-80GB) with async KV-cache warming during low-traffic windows. Failover time target: <120s for routing switch.

Autoscale & burst policy proposal:
- Baseline autoscale: based on GPU utilization + queued requests. Scale-up trigger: sustained avg GPU util > 60% for 60s OR queued requests > 40 for 90s. Scale-down: util < 30% for 120s.
- Burst lane: allow 2x baseline capacity for short bursts up to 15 minutes, gated by a token-bucket budget per day. If burst budget is exhausted, fall back to throttling with graceful 429 + retry headers. Burst lanes limited to non-spot capacity for guaranteed latency.
- Canary plan: 48-hour canary with 10% traffic split to hosted fallback for the first 24h, then 100% to Dedicated if metrics stable. Canary SLOs: 95th pct latency <= 250ms, error rate <0.5%.

Operational notes:
- Networking: need VPC peering + subnet allocation in eu-west-1 (customer owns routing controls).
- Logs: enable token-level billing traces and per-token latency sampling for root-cause during canary.

I've attached a sizing estimate (pool-sizing-estimate.xlsx) with cost delta vs. pure US primary. Quick summary: EU primary increases baseline monthly cost ~14% vs US primary but meets PHI residency reqs.

If folks are aligned I can open the provisioning ticket and request capacity reservation for Nov 30 cutover.

- Karthik
Engineering Manager, Runtime & Orchestration
karthik@redwood.ai

Team — thanks for the fast turn. Summary & agreed actions: 

Decisions (agreed):
- Region: EU primary (eu-west-1) for PHI; US warm-standby (us-west-2). Owner: Karthik.
- Scaling: use Karthik's autoscale thresholds (scale-up at util >60% / queue >40).
- Burst: token-bucket gated 2x baseline for up to 15m bursts; guaranteed non-spot capacity for bursts.
- Canary: 48-hour canary with production-weighted traffic. Traffic split: 90% Dedicated / 10% hosted fallback first 24h, then 100% if stable.
- Compliance deliverables: include audit log list and KMS rotation cadence in the runbook. Owner: Monica + Rishi.

Action items & timeline:
- Karthik: open provisioning ticket and reserve capacity in eu-west-1 (4 nodes) + us-west-2 (2 nodes) by Mon Nov 23.
- Monica: draft implementation-runbook-v1.pdf with canary checklist, SLOs, rollback plan, and compliance checklist by Fri Nov 27.
- Rishi: confirm alerting thresholds and add token-level billing traces by Nov 24.
- FlowHealth (Olivia/Samir): sign SOW and confirm procurement terms by Nov 26.

I'll attach the runbook and push DocuSign for SOW once Monica posts the runbook. If anyone needs a quick sync, I'm available Fri 9-10am PT.

Thanks — moving to provisioning ticket once Karthik confirms reservation.

Laura Bennett
